lensName: Prof. Margaret Morse lens: inhabited systems
rationale: The portfolio preserves an explicit, source-bounded connection among artistic, civic, technical, and social practice while keeping Jamie's technical-project and implementation role prominent. Three distinct project continuities show people influencing, inhabiting, remembering, and continuing systems. The proof is unusually concrete in the residency/gathering handoffs, WOWList's organizer-language model and historical use, and the coalition's room-to-public-system practice.

individuallyAssessableRequirements.requirement: A visible threshold within two clicks connects artistic, civic, technical, and social practice while supporting the target role.
individuallyAssessableRequirements.evidence: /about opens with the technical project manager and implementation lead role, then Systems people can inhabit names all four dimensions and links to project evidence. Desktop one click; mobile Menu then About.

individuallyAssessableRequirements.requirement: At least three public-safe project continuities demonstrate experimentation, participation, attention, documentation, care, place, or hospitality.
individuallyAssessableRequirements.evidence: The threeProjectTrace below reconstructs WOWList, Sunday Dinner/196, and NYCAC/FairRentNYC from the project pages and checked canonical boundaries.

individuallyAssessableRequirements.requirement: Readers can explain how these systems differ from conventional administration.
individuallyAssessableRequirements.evidence: Community vocabulary defines the platform's model; artist needs shape space and access; collective questions shape campaign pathways and recoverable records. Participants can influence and carry on the work.

individuallyAssessableRequirements.requirement: Collective credit, privacy, protected educational records, and testimonial boundaries are preserved.
individuallyAssessableRequirements.evidence: Public project credits, source-note boundaries, the active Open House claim, held coursework claim, and reviewed rendered text provide the bounded audit recorded above.

evidence.finding: Systems people can inhabit links a ten-day, collectively governed gallery experiment to the recurring question of relationships, participation, memory, and continuation.
The same prose and project links remain readable in a single mobile column.
Two explicitly redacted reconstructions show how hospitality and artist agency become usable workflows.
The website was one part of the room pairs public campaign surfaces, a working circle, and a collective public gathering.
The current public threshold photograph and dated historical product narrative keep digital interface and gathering connected.
The Open House source is dated June 28, 2006, and expressly denies sole authorship, renewed participant publicity, complete attendance, and long-term outcomes.

Natural-language contributions and followable keyword communities make participation possible across calendars, websites, and email; public support and an independently published tutorial let organizers learn and continue using the system.
threeProjectTrace.inhabitedSystem: People supply the language and contributions that organize the interface, rather than merely receiving a centrally edited list.
threeProjectTrace.evidence: Product decision; What became usable; Product practice in one view; source notes 3-7 and the 2016 Sunday Dinner event route.
threeProjectTrace.creditAndLimit: Jamie and Richard co-built it, with organizers and participants credited. Historical adoption is distinct from the small 2026 tester threshold.
